text:
marta: Quick sync: proposing 'dual-attach' mode - tenant keeps private endpoint + peering. Want clear failover precedence, simple API toggle, and lightweight agent behavior. Thoughts?

omar: sounds useful. we need a single source of truth for preference to avoid split-brain. cp-managed by default?

trina: cp-managed for Dedicated; customer-managed for Private. expose `attach_pref` enum: ["endpoint_first","peer_first","endpoint_only","peer_only"].

jess: what triggers a failover? tcp loss? tls failure? auth 401? define a health tuple.

marta: health = tcp + tls + auth_check. if any fails continuously for 30s -> fail to peer. re-enable endpoint after 90s healthy. add 15s jitter to probes.

ben: observability: emit `attachment.current`, `attachment.last_fail_ts`, `attachment.fail_reason`, `attachment.switch_count`. alert if >3 switches in 15m. tag traces with `attachment_path` and `attachment_id`.

sre-bot: note: probe interval currently 10s. updating semantics requires runbook edit and deploy checklist.

omar: security: ensure identical token scope across paths. if agent does switching, token refresh must be atomic to avoid 401 storms.

trina: rollout: internal pilot -> 1 low-traffic customer -> 2-week monitor window. provide UI toggle and audit log for manual overrides.

marta: ok I'll draft RFC follow-up with enum, probe thresholds, API sample (/v1/attachments/{id}/pref), metrics, and rollout checklist. tagging reviewers: @omar @trina @jess.
